summary: Extends LDAP with absolute True and False filters, based on capabilities in X.500, and extends the string form of search filters to support them. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: Two search rules that always match everything or nothing, which are handy as building blocks.

questions: what is the ldap true filter
how to publish ldap absolute true false support
subtitle: LDAP search filters that always evaluate to True or False, written (&) and (|).

tldr.problem: X.500 supports absolute True and False assertions, but they were left out of LDAPv3 because the LDAPv2 string form could not represent empty 'and' and 'or' filters.
tldr.mechanism: LDAP allows 'and' and 'or' filters with zero elements: an empty 'and' is True and written (&), an empty 'or' is False and written (|).
tldr.outcome: This enables a more direct mapping between DAP and LDAP, as needed for DAP-to-LDAP gateways.

today: RFC 4526 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Background
sections.content:
The X.500 Directory Access Protocol supports absolute True and False assertions: an and filter with zero elements is always True and an or filter with zero elements is always False. They are commonly used when requesting DSA-specific entries that may lack objectClass attributes, where (objectClass=*) may evaluate to False.

LDAPv2 placed no limit on the number of elements, but its string form could not represent empty sets, so absolute filters were unfortunately eliminated from LDAPv3. This document restores them.
sections.plainLanguage: Older systems had an 'always yes' and 'always no' question, but they were dropped by accident. This brings them back.

sections.title: Absolute True and False Filters
sections.content:
Implementations of this extension SHALL allow and and or with zero filter elements. An empty and SHALL evaluate to True and is written (&). An empty or SHALL evaluate to False and is written (|).

Servers supporting the feature SHOULD publish the OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.5.3 as a value of the supportedFeatures attribute in the root DSE. Clients SHOULD NOT use the feature unless they know the server supports it.
sections.plainLanguage: An empty 'all of these' is vacuously true and an empty 'any of these' is false. Ask a server first before using them.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The (re)introduction of these filters is not believed to raise any new security considerations. The IANA registered the feature, and the OID was assigned by the OpenLDAP Foundation under its private enterprise allocation.

Certain searches, such as those retrieving subschema information, require particular filters, and this document does not change that.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new to worry about, and other required searches work the same as before.
